A census measures the world THROUGH that code. Same thousand worlds, same
values, different readout implementation. The `perf:` claim holds at population
scale, which is the scale it needed to hold at and the one nothing else checks.

I HAD THE RIGHT IDEA AND THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, and the wrong one would have
told you nothing. I said census 4's own report would be the controlled read. It
is not: the queue reports a census as a diff against the CAMPAIGN TIP's
committed goldens, and those never moved -- census 3 was delivered on a branch
and never merged -- so census 4 reported "125 goldens moved", the identical
count census 3 reported, from the identical stale baseline. Two runs, same
number, and it means nothing about the code between them. THE COMPARISON THAT
WORKS IS OUTPUT AGAINST OUTPUT: both census branches carry computed values, so
diff those directly and the baseline cancels.

That is the second time today the same distinction decided an answer -- the
first was the-wanderers' two censuses, also byte-identical, which is how we
learned the-staple-r3's history_bake work was projection over committed state.
A delivered census branch is a MEASUREMENT you can compare against another
measurement. Its queue row is a bookkeeping diff and is not that.

WHAT EACH OF YOU GETS FROM IT:

just on the seeds your suite runs. Worth a chronicle line; you already merged.

underworld-peoples: the 125 goldens both your censuses move are YOUR campaign's
delta against main, and none of it is absorbed drift. Your census 4 is the one
to land. Your autonym cache remains separately unmeasured -- it sits on both
sides of this comparison and cancels; the two-build `cmp` at 6be88ddc6 vs
385261d98 is still the only thing that settles it.

the-wanderers: this is the result I told you to wait for before resubmitting.
